The Health Care PRICE Transparency Act (H.R. 267) is a critical step toward exposing Big Pharma's rigged pricing schemes. Requiring hospitals to publish machine-readable charge lists and insurers to disclose negotiated rates forces daylight into a system where bureaucrats and corporate middlemen profit from opacity.

But let's be clear: Transparency alone won't fix a system where Medicaid wastes billions on fraudulent provider taxes and hospitals game reimbursement rates through state-directed payment loopholes. The real issue? D.C. enables this looting through complex billing codes and bloated contracts that prioritize insurer-pharmacy backroom deals over patient costs.

Until we slash the administrative bloat fueling these schemes, transparency just gives taxpayers a clearer view of the theft.

The Health Care PRICE Transparency Act (H.R. 267) proves Tennessee's push for upfront pricing aligns with federal efforts, but real-world execution remains shaky. While the Tennessee Right to Shop Act (2019) and 2024's Prior Authorization Fairness Act show progress, Patient Rights Advocate reports only 12% hospital compliance statewide – exposing the gap between policy and practice.

The Fair Tax Act's machine-readable files should empower consumers, yet opaque algorithms and percentage-based pricing still let hospitals hide true costs. Baptist Memorial's estimator tool demonstrates functional transparency models, but systemic enforcement lags.

Until CMS cracks down on noncompliant hospitals and mandates dollar-specific pricing over vague formulas, Tennessee families will keep playing billing roulette. Real reform requires teeth – not just spreadsheets buried on hospital websites.

The real story is in the enforcement failures and hidden costs—see the full breakdown: https://t.co/h7kooYDiOg
